mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, preserve the signed subtraction order on both sides, i.e., interpret (A - B) = (C - D) exactly as written. Without this, you may swap terms or take absolute values, leading to incorrect equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states that the difference between two persons' counts equals the difference between two other persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D| or swapping to (B - A) = (C - D).

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable’s numeric value becomes known, immediately substitute it into every pending equation and update any dependent variables. Without this, equations remain unsolved and later constraints cannot be satisfied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After assigning a concrete number to a person (via direct count, transfer, or solved equation).
mathgap.example: Leaving an equation X - Y = 5 unchanged after learning X = 10, instead of substituting to find Y = 5.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement (e.g., 'A has K more than B') using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after all earlier transfers and direct counts have been applied. Without this, you may use outdated values and obtain wrong equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a comparative sentence in the order it appears.
mathgap.example: Using B's original count to evaluate 'A has 3 more than B' even though a prior transfer increased B's count.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and ignore unrelated statements. Without this, you waste effort on irrelevant constraints and may become confused.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, after parsing all statements, to isolate the relevant subsystem for the query.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve for X while also processing equations about unrelated persons Y and Z that never connect to X.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique capitalized token as a separate variable, even if two names differ by only a single character, to avoid conflating distinct persons. Without this, you may merge two different people's counts, causing incorrect equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears in the narrative.
mathgap.example: Confusing 'Ada' with 'Adam' and using the same variable for both.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret phrases like 'the difference between the number of X that A and B have' as the signed subtraction A - B, preserving the order given. Without this, you may take the absolute difference or reverse the order, leading to sign errors.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement references the difference between two persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Reading 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| or as B - A instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Translate 'A has K more (fewer) items than B' into the signed equation A - B = K (or A - B = ‑K for 'fewer'). Without this, you may reverse the subtraction or ignore the sign, producing wrong relationships.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative phrase with 'more' or 'fewer'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 3 more than B' as B - A = 3.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N items', assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X. Without this, earlier counts may incorrectly persist and conflict with later information.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count sentence appears.
mathgap.example: Keeping X = 5 from an earlier statement even after later reading 'X has 12 items'.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application (Bidirectional)
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement 'X gives K items to Y' appears, immediately subtract K from X and add K to Y, using the current counts at that moment. Without this, you may apply the transfer out of order or ignore the giver's reduction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a transfer sentence in the narrative order.
mathgap.example: Adding K to Y without subtracting K from X, or applying the transfer after later statements.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Difference Equality Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two signed differences (e.g., '(A - B) = (C - D)'), evaluate the equality using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative. Without this, you may use values that have changed later, violating the intended constraint.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a difference‑equality sentence in order.
mathgap.example: Using a later updated count for A when evaluating '(A - B) = (C - D)' that appeared earlier.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often misinterprets 'A has K more than B' as B - A = K, reversing the subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map 'has K more' to A - B = K (or A - B = ‑K for 'fewer').

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign and uses |A - B|, losing information about which person has more.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order and sign when interpreting 'difference between' phrases or equality of differences.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers after later statements or treats them as simultaneous without respecting the narrative order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, updating both giver and receiver before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct count is a permanent initial value, ignoring later overrides.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, assign the value at that point and overwrite any previous value for that person.

mathgap.description: Ignoring chronological order when evaluating difference equality statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model evaluates a difference equality using counts after later changes, violating the intended timing.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a difference‑equality appears, evaluate it using the current counts at that exact point in the narrative.
